review_note: Reviewed by reading tests/testthat/test-gamma-labelled-q2-sd-b32.R line by line. (1) The oracle is independent: a base-R dense Laplace marginal (gb32_oracle) with a hand-built non-unit-diagonal relmat K and cov2cor(ape::vcv(tree)) for phylo, evaluated at the fitted beta, shape, SD curves and fitted rho. The package tip-covariance helper is only compared against that hand kernel. Console oracle gaps are 1.3e-10 to 1.5e-10 against a 1e-4 tolerance. (2) Emulated-bug sensitivity is asserted at >0.1 per bug, covering swapped SD formulas, reversed SD vectors, rho dropped, rho sign flipped, kernel by level position, cov2cor(K), supplied-order and raw vcv. The smallest gap in the log is 0.76 (raw_vcv_not_correlation). (3) All six linked row_keys are fitted: mu:I and mu:x1 for phylo/tree, relmat/K and relmat/Q, with the labelled (1 + x | p | id) block and one SD formula per coefficient, so the rho-linked pair is fitted jointly. The test refuses slope-only and unlabelled forms. The Q route is checked in the test only by logLik equality with the K fit at 1e-4. I ran a scratch Q fit on Totoro (cores 358-359, now finished): its logLik matched the dense oracle with K = solve(Q) to 1.3e-10, and dropping rho moved the oracle by 21.7. So the Q rows are directly oracle-backed. (4) I recomputed every sha256 from the current files: test file, R/drmTMB.R, R/methods.R, R/random-effect-targets.R, src/drmTMB.cpp, receipt, manifest and console log all match the receipt and manifest.
